_comment_family: The other end of the same family, and the reason both packs declare a
full name instead of 'Raleway': the two files share name ID 1, so the
family alone names neither of them - and the name it does not name
them with is one the interface has already claimed. See the note in
raleway-regular.json, which this pack is the other half of; both
halves of that argument apply here unchanged.
Weight 700, which is the file's own usWeightClass and what the cut is
called. Asking for 800 or 900 on the strength of how loud a highlight
should be would invite a browser to synthesise a heavier face on top
of one that already has its own weight - and synthesised bold is the
one kind of emphasis that cannot be measured, since the smear it adds
is not in any metric the layout reads.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the Windows full name (name ID 4) and the second the
PostScript name; both name this one cut rather than the family, so a
machine answering to either is answering with a Bold - which is the
whole of what this face is for. 'Raleway' on its own is deliberately
absent: the Regular answers to it, and so does the interface's own
webfont, and either one arriving here would be the highlight silently
_comment_stack: Damage limitation, and a highlight's stack has one duty beyond the
usual: it must not end up drawing a picked word exactly as the words
either side of it are drawn - a failure that draws no attention to
itself, which is the kind this app has been bitten by before (see
american-typewriter-itc-pro-bold).
That duty is discharged differently here than in marydale-bold, and
it is worth being plain about why. There the difference between block
and highlight was a HAND - two unrelated families - so the two stacks
had to stay apart entry by entry or the distinction vanished. Here the
difference is a WEIGHT, and weight travels in the font string beside
the family rather than inside it (see textProps in js/text.js): this
face is asked for at 700 and the block's at 400, so the two may share
every fallback and still come out heavy against light. Falling through
to the same family is the correct outcome rather than the failure it
would be next door.
So the entries are the block's, and each is reached at 700. 'Raleway'
second is the interface's own vendored webfont, which declares a real
700 among its five weights (frontend/vendor/raleway.css), so a missing
file leaves both the typeface and the contrast intact. Segoe UI is on
every Windows this app runs on and has a Bold; Arial is the floor and
has one too. Impact and Arial Black are absent for the block's reason -
they are heavy display grotesques and this is a text sans - and for one
more: a picked word in Impact inside a line of Segoe would not read as
emphasis but as a second channel.
